stem: A 7-year-old undergoing obesity assessment has height, weight and BMI recorded; which additional anthropometric finding is associated with increased cardiometabolic risk in children older than 6 years?

options.text: Waist circumference measured without using a ratio

explanation: Waist-to-height ratio greater than 0.5 is associated with increased cardiometabolic risk in children older than 6 years.
rationale: This item tests recognition of an obesity-related anthropometric risk marker. In children older than 6 years, a waist-to-height ratio above 0.5 is the relevant finding linked with higher cardiometabolic risk.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because a waist-to-height ratio greater than 0.5 is the anthropometric marker associated with increased cardiometabolic risk in children older than 6 years.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because waist circumference alone is not the specific risk threshold given; the relevant measure is the waist-to-height ratio.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because pregnancy details are part of history taking, not an anthropometric risk marker.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because weekend versus weekday sleep variation is a sleep history feature, not an anthropometric finding.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because sweet drink intake is a dietary history factor, not an anthropometric measure.
